subject.title: fix(irc): disconnect on oversized inbound lines

question: Should an oversized inbound IRC record immediately disconnect the channel, and if so must this PR also prove or fix gateway lifecycle recovery and status after the socket closes?
rationale: The protocol supports a strict 512-byte limit, but fail-closed behavior changes compatibility for previously tolerated servers and the current proof stops at the client socket rather than the channel lifecycle.

options.title: Keep Strict Disconnect With Lifecycle Proof
options.body: Retain the RFC limit and require a gateway-level test showing that the account stops or reconnects correctly after the protocol-triggered close.

options.title: Accept Client-Only Disconnect
options.body: Merge the current behavior while accepting that a noncompliant record may leave IRC unavailable until the channel or gateway is restarted.

options.title: Bound And Discard The Record
options.body: Replace disconnection with a bounded discard-until-newline state if compatibility is preferred over fail-closed protocol enforcement.

recommendation.title: Keep Strict Disconnect With Lifecycle Proof
recommendation.body: Retain the RFC limit and require a gateway-level test showing that the account stops or reconnects correctly after the protocol-triggered close.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged IRC client review and integration history makes this person the strongest available owner for the compatibility and lifecycle choice.
